description:
Build Elixir mode as decided in 'Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?' (defk-dtw.6) and 'How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?' (defk-dtw.16).

- A compile-time transform that generates real Elixir source from each kernel body (no IR interpreter): x[i] reads the packed binary, len/alloc map to binary ops, writes rebind an array threaded through loops and ifs.
- Limits are applied, so agreement can be exact: i64 range checked after every integer op (ArithmeticError), array writes and narrow element types raise when the value doesn't fit, out-of-range indices raise the same module as the kernel (Enum.OutOfBoundsError), and wrong-typed arguments raise ArgumentError like the kernel.
- Entry points: generated Mod.__defk_elixir__/2 per kernel; config :defk, mode: :elixir allowed only in :dev/:test (default native); always compiled in :test.
- yield/timing don't exist in Elixir mode.

Done when every existing test kernel and catalog kernel compiles in Elixir mode, and dbg/IO.inspect work inside a kernel body in Elixir mode.
title: Build Elixir mode
